chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: Artificial intelligence (AI) for skin-disease classification has advanced rapidly, driven by large public archives such as ISIC and HAM10000. These archives are, however, narrow in two aspects: they are dominated by lighter skin tones and by neoplastic (cancer-related) conditions captured with dermoscopy. The settings where AI-assisted dermatology could have the greatest impact-resourceconstrained primary-care and teledermatology clinicsdiffer from this training regime on both counts simultaneously.
chk_problem.reason: The poster accurately describes the research problem of decomposing the generalization gap in dermatology AI models, focusing on skin tone and disease-distribution shift.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: We use four public datasets, each assigned a specific experimental role (Table 1). Source domain (in-domain reference): HAM10000 and ISIC 2019 are pooled and mapped to a shared eight-class neoplastic taxonomy to train and evaluate the cancer baseline on familiar data. Tone-isolation. DDI holds diagnosis broadly fixed while varying skin tone, isolating the tone effect; we use its binary malignant/benign label. Distribution-isolation. SCIN is tone-diverse but dominated by non-neoplastic conditions absent from cancer training data, isolating the distribution effect.
chk_method.reason: The poster outlines the method of evaluating models using frozen embeddings and datasets assigned specific experimental roles, consistent with the reference.

chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Distribution shift dominates across all evaluated models. The cancer baseline degrades sharply from its in-domain performance to unfamiliar conditions (a drop from 0.62 to 0.21 balanced accuracy across clinical categories), a far larger effect than the withindisease skin-tone gap, which is comparatively small (0.10-0.18) and did not show a consistent direction.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: Using only public data and free-tier compute, we decomposed the dermatology-AI generalization gap and found disease-distribution shift to dominate skin tone, traced the effect to a representational deficit in cancerspecialized models, and found that cheap adaptation is most effective when the starting representation already encodes the target conditions.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster accurately concludes that disease-distribution shift dominates the generalization gap and highlights the benefits of dermatology foundation models for cheap adaptation.
